'''Esteban Matías Cambiasso Deleau''' ({{IPA|es|esˈteβaŋ kamˈbjaso}};{{efn|In isolation, ''Esteban'' is pronounced {{IPA|es|esˈteβan|}}.}} born 18 August 1980), nicknamed ''"Cuchu"'',{{efn|{{IPA|es|ˈkutʃu}}}} is an Argentine former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[midfielder]].

During his career, Cambiasso won 21 official titles, the majority of which were won during his ten seasons at [[Inter Milan]], including five ''[[Scudetto|Scudetti]]'' and the [[2009–10 UEFA Champions League]].

A full international from 2000 to 2011, Cambiasso won 52 [[Cap (sport)|caps]] for [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]] and represented the country at the [[2006 FIFA World Cup|2006 World Cup]], the [[2005 FIFA Confederations Cup|2005 Confederations Cup]], and at the [[Copa América]] in [[2007 Copa América|2007]] and [[2011 Copa América|2011]].

==Club career==

===Early career===
Cambiasso began his professional career with [[Argentinos Juniors]] in 1995, moving to [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]] in 1996 along with his brother [[Nicolás Cambiasso]]. In 1998, he moved back to Argentina, where he played for three years with [[Club Atlético Independiente|Independiente]] and one with [[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]]. With some good experience under his belt, he returned to Real Madrid in 2002. He helped ''Los Blancos'' win the [[UEFA Super Cup]] and the [[Intercontinental Cup (1960–2004)|Intercontinental Cup]] in 2002, and the [[2002–03 La Liga|Liga]] and the [[Supercopa de España]] in 2003, also reaching the semi-finals of the [[2002–03 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]] that season. Cambiasso also reached the [[2004 Copa del Rey Final|Copa del Rey final]] the following season.

===Inter Milan===
[[File:Cambiasso Inter 2013.jpg|thumb|upright|Cambiasso training with Inter in 2013]]

In July 2004, Cambiasso signed with [[Serie A]] club [[Inter Milan]] after his contract with Real Madrid expired in June.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11860/2387312/cambiasso-signs-inter-deal |title=Cambiasso signs Inter deal |work=Sky Sports |access-date=5 April 2014 }}</ref> He helped Inter win the [[Coppa Italia]] during his first season with the club,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://interfc.it/Coppaitalia.asp |title=INTER – LE VITTORIE IN COPPA ITALIA |work=Internazionale |access-date=28 August 2014 |language=it |archive-date=4 January 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170104204613/http://www.interfc.it/Coppaitalia.asp |url-status=dead }}</ref> playing regularly as a defensive midfielder, partnered in the middle of Inter's midfield with fellow Argentine [[Juan Sebastián Verón]]. In Italy, he became known as one of the outstanding players of the 2004–05 season, along with [[A.C. Milan|Milan]]'s [[Kaká]].

During the return match of the [[2006 Coppa Italia Final]], Cambiasso scored an impressive goal, the first of the match, for the 3–1 victory over [[A.S. Roma|Roma]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.inter.it/en/match_center/3585 |title=Inter 3–1 Roma |work=Internazionale |access-date=28 August 2014 }}</ref> On 9 September 2006, he scored twice in the opening game of the season, with Inter defeating [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]] 3–2. On 7 November 2007, he along with [[Zlatan Ibrahimović]] scored a brace apiece to defeat [[PFC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]] 4–2 in the [[2007–08 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/01c7-0e6eb633aa04-da4b818b8a1a-1000--inter-comeback-eliminates-cska/ |title=Inter comeback eliminates CSKA |publisher=UEFA |date=7 November 2007 |access-date=5 April 2014 }}</ref> On 23 December, Cambiasso scored the winning goal for Inter as they came from behind to defeat city rivals Milan 2–1 in the [[Derby della Madonnina]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2007/12/23/italy/serie-a/fc-internazionale-milano/ac-milan/501248/ |title=Internazionale vs. Milan 2–1 |publisher=Soccerway |date=23 December 2007 |access-date=6 April 2014 }}</ref>

On 23 March 2009, it was announced that Inter and Cambiasso had come to terms about a contract renewal, extending his contract at the club until 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/10/italy/2009/03/23/1170922/official-esteban-cambiasso-signs-new-deal-with-inter |title=Official: Esteban Cambiasso Signs New Deal With Inter |publisher=Goal |date=23 March 2009 |access-date=5 April 2014 }}</ref> He was very important in the [[2009–10 UEFA Champions League]] win as well, scoring the second goal of a 2–1 victory over [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] at the [[San Siro]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/8530208.stm |title=Chelsea suffered a first leg defeat to former boss Jose Mourinho's Inter Milan in their Champions League last 16 tie. |publisher=BBC Sport |date=24 February 2010 |access-date=5 April 2014 }}</ref> a result which ultimately helped Inter go on to win the final, 2–0, against [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] on 22 May 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/europe/8697017.stm |title=Jose Mourinho wrote his name into the history books as Diego Milito inspired Inter Milan to Champions League glory against Bayern Munich at the Bernabeu. |publisher=BBC Sport |date=22 May 2010 |access-date=5 April 2014 }}</ref> In a [[2010–11 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] match against [[FC Twente|Twente]] on 24 November, Cambiasso scored the game's only goal, securing a place in the knockout round for the holders.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/01eb-0e765737d182-5fba73a3c74a-1000--cambiasso-strike-takes-inter-into-knockout-stage/ |title=Cambiasso strike takes Inter into knockout stage |publisher=UEFA |date=24 November 2010 |access-date=6 April 2014 }}</ref> On 9 January 2011, Cambiasso scored twice as Inter came from a goal down to defeat [[Catania Calcio|Catania]] 2–1.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.goal.com/en/match/48854/catania-vs-inter-milan/report |title=Catania 1–2 Inter: Esteban Cambiasso Brace Completes Comeback For Leonardo's Second Successive Victory |publisher=Goal |date=9 January 2011 |access-date=6 April 2014 |archive-date=21 January 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110121033352/http://www.goal.com/en/match/48854/catania-vs-inter-milan/report |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Cambiasso received the first red card of his Inter career on 30 March 2013 for a reckless tackle on [[Sebastian Giovinco]]; he was suspended for one match.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.espnfc.com/news/story/_/id/1395889/inter-milan-midfielder-esteban-cambiasso-suspended-for-one-match?cc=5739 |title=Cambiasso suspended for one match |publisher=ESPN FC |date=1 April 2013 |access-date=29 May 2014}}</ref> On 22 September 2013, Cambiasso scored Inter's sixth goal in their 7–0 hammering of newly promoted club [[U.S. Sassuolo Calcio|Sassuolo]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en-us/match/119162/sassuolo-vs-inter/report |title=Sassuolo 0–7 Inter: Nerazzurri storm to rampant win |publisher=Goal |date=22 September 2013 |access-date=5 April 2014 }}</ref> Four days later, Cambiasso helped Inter come from a goal down at home to Fiorentina, scoring Inter's first goal in their 2–1 victory.

At the end of the [[2013–14 Serie A|2013–14 season]], Cambiasso left Inter as his contract expired and he was not offered an extension. Technical director [[Piero Ausilio]] said, "He waited for our decision until now, and for that he must be thanked, but I'm convinced that in his future he'll have a role at Inter."<ref>{{cite news|last=Carminati|first=Nadi|title=Transfer news: Inter confirm Esteban Cambiasso will leave San Siro at end of season|url=https://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11860/9316059/transfer-news-inter-confirm-esteban-cambiasso-will-leave-san-siro-at-end-of-season|access-date=18 May 2014|publisher=Sky Sports |date=18 May 2014}}</ref>

===Leicester City===
[[File:Esteban Cambiasso 2015.jpg|thumb|upright|Cambiasso playing for Leicester City in 2015]]

On 28 August 2014, Cambiasso signed a one-year deal with newly promoted [[Premier League]] club [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]], joining on a free transfer, having been released by Inter at the end of their [[2013–14 Inter Milan season|2013–14 season]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Esteban Cambiasso Signs For Leicester City|url=https://www.lcfc.com/news/article/280814-esteban-cambiasso-signs-for-leicester-city-1882324.aspx|access-date=28 August 2014|publisher=Leicester City F.C.|date=28 August 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11712/9445278/transfer-news-leicester-sign-esteban-cambiasso-on-one-year-contract |title=Transfer news: Leicester sign Esteban Cambiasso on one-year contract |work=Sky Sports |date=28 August 2014 |access-date=28 August 2014 }}</ref> In his first interview since joining the club, Cambiasso cited the club's desperate pursuit of him and the lure of Premier League football as the reasons he signed.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/leicester-city/11064127/Esteban-Cambiasso-says-lure-of-the-Premier-League-behind-decision-to-join-Leicester-City.html |title=Esteban Cambiasso says lure of the Premier League behind decision to join Leicester City |work=The Daily Telegraph |date=29 August 2014 |access-date=30 August 2014 }}</ref> He was called up for his first game three days after signing, a 1–1 draw at the [[King Power Stadium]] against [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], as an unused substitute.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Whalley|first1=Mike|title=Leicester 1–1 Arsenal|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28917059|access-date=31 August 2014|publisher=BBC Sport|date=31 August 2014}}</ref> Cambiasso made his debut for Leicester on 13 September against [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]], coming on as a half-time substitute and impressing in the club's 1–0 win, their first of the league season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/29090535 |title=Leonardo Ulloa scored his third goal of the season to earn Nigel Pearson's Leicester side their first win since they returned to the Premier League. |publisher=BBC Sport |date=13 September 2014 |access-date=13 September 2014 }}</ref> His first goal was an equaliser as Leicester beat [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] 5–3 at home after trailing 1–3 with 30 minutes to play.<ref>{{cite news|title=Leicester 5–3 Man Utd|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29196081|access-date=21 September 2014|publisher=BBC Sport|date=21 September 2014}}</ref> Cambiasso scored his second goal of the season, an opener in the fourth minute following an assist from [[Leonardo Ulloa]], in a 3–2 loss against [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]] at [[Loftus Road]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hafez |first1=Shamoon |title=Queens Park Rangers 3-2 Leicester City |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/30156605 |access-date=6 September 2020 |work=BBC Sport |date=29 November 2014}}</ref> That was Leicester's first goal in 504 minutes without scoring, or 56 days.<ref>{{cite news|title=QPR 3–2 Leicester: Match Report|url=https://www.football.co.uk/queens_park_rangers/qpr_3-2_leicester__match_report_rss5175058.shtml#ffX3I8OtVmeC4wMe.97|access-date=29 November 2014|publisher=Football.co.uk|date=29 November 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=QPR's Charlie Austin supplies a lift as Leicester City hit the skids|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/nov/29/qpr-leicester-city-premier-league-match-report|access-date=29 November 2014|work=The Guardian|date=29 November 2014}}</ref> On 4 April 2015, Cambiasso gave Leicester a 12th-minute lead against [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] in a game that ''the Foxes'' would go on to win 2–1, their first league victory in eight matches, stretching back to 10 January 2015.<ref>{{cite news|title=Leicester City 2–1 West Ham United|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32097799|access-date=16 May 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=4 April 2015}}</ref> This started a run of seven wins and one draw from Leicester's final nine Premier League fixtures, with the team finishing 14th in the table.<ref name=qpr>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/32770769|title=Leicester 5–1 QPR|date=24 May 2015|publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref>

On 18 May 2015, at Leicester City's annual awards, Cambiasso's impressive performances over the course of the season saw him pick up the Player of the Year award, as voted by the club's supporters.<ref name="Leicester City">{{cite news|title=Esteban Cambiasso Named Leicester City Player Of The Year|url=https://www.lcfc.com/news/article/esteban-cambiasso-named-leicester-city-player-of-the-year-2461984.aspx|access-date=18 May 2015|work=Leicester City|date=18 May 2015}}</ref> On 24 May, Cambiasso scored in a 5–1 defeat of QPR in Leicester's final match of the Premier League season.<ref name=qpr/>

On 21 July 2015, it was announced that Cambiasso had been offered a new deal by the club, but turned the contract down, and he would be leaving the club.<ref>{{cite web|title=Esteban Cambiasso announces he is leaving Leicester City|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11712/9920222/esteban-cambiasso-announces-he-is-leaving-leicester-city|publisher=Sky Sports|access-date=3 August 2015|date=3 August 2015}}</ref>

===Olympiacos===
On 7 August 2015, Cambiasso signed a two-year deal with Greek giants [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympiacos.org/article/50049/paiktis-toy-olympiakoy-o-kampiaso|title=Cambiasso signs Olympiacos deal |date=7 August 2015 |publisher=Olympiacos.org|access-date=7 August 2015}}</ref> He scored his first goal for them on 2 December in a 4–0 away win against [[Panegialios F.C.|Panegialios]] in the group stage of the [[Greek Football Cup|Greek Cup]]. He scored twice in 14 [[Super League Greece]] games as the [[Piraeus]]-based side retained their title, including the equaliser in a 3–1 home win over [[Panathinaikos F.C.|Panathinaikos]] in the [[Derby of the eternal enemies]] on 13 March 2016.<ref>{{cite news|title=Olympiakos 3–1 Panathinaikos|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/35749253|access-date=14 March 2017|publisher=BBC Sport|date=13 March 2016}}</ref> Eleven days earlier, the first leg of the cup semi-final against [[PAOK FC|PAOK]], he scored in a 2–1 away win which was abandoned due to violence by the local fans.<ref>{{cite news|title=Violence sees Greek Cup semi-final abandoned|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/35713358|access-date=14 March 2017|publisher=BBC Sport|date=2 March 2016}}</ref>

Cambiassio renewed his contract on 11 July 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympiacos.org/article/58782/epektasi-synergasias-me-ton-estempan-kampiaso|title=Contract extension of Esteban Cambiasso |date=11 July 2016 |publisher=Olympiacos.org|access-date=11 July 2016}}</ref> On 9 March 2017, he returned to the starting lineup as a result of the dismissal of Olympiacos manager [[Paulo Bento]] against [[Beşiktaş J.K.|Beşiktaş]] for the first leg of the [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Europa League round of 16 stage]], and headed the opening goal of a 1–1 draw, subsequently being named [[man of the match]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Outstanding Cambiasso not enough for the Reds|url=http://www.ekathimerini.com/216774/article/ekathimerini/sports/outstanding-cambiasso-not-enough-for-the-reds|access-date=14 March 2017|work=Ekathimerini|date=10 March 2017}}</ref>

===Retirement===
On 8 September 2017, Cambiasso announced his retirement from professional football, two months after his contract with Olympiacos expired. Cambiasso's success in the official [[UEFA A Licence]] examinations in [[Centro Tecnico Federale di Coverciano|Coverciano]], subsequently allowing him to take up an assistant role in [[Serie A]] or [[Serie B|B]] or head coach role [[Serie C]] in the future, influenced his decision to retire from the game.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newsit.gr/athlitika/podosfairo/olympiakos-antio-ston-megalo-kampiaso/2210437/|script-title=el:Ολυμπιακός: "Αντίο" στον μεγάλο Καμπιάσο|date=8 September 2017|work=Newsit.gr|access-date=8 September 2017|language=el-GR}}</ref><ref>{{cite press release|url=https://www.figc.it/it/federazione/news/nuovi-allenatori-professionisti-uefa-a-tra-gli-abilitati-anche-patrizia-panico/|title=Nuovi allenatori professionisti UEFA A: tra gli abilitati anche Patrizia Panico|date=7 September 2017|access-date=13 February 2019|publisher=Italian Football Federation (FIGC)|language=it}}</ref>

==International career==
[[File:Argentine - Portugal - Esteban Cambiasso.jpg|thumb|upright|Esteban Cambiasso during a friendly match between Argentina and [[Portugal national football team|Portugal]] in Geneva, Switzerland on 9 February 2011]]

Cambiasso first represented [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]] in the youth squads, along with national teammates [[Juan Román Riquelme]], [[Pablo Aimar]], [[Walter Samuel]] and others. He was in the squads for the [[1997 FIFA World Youth Championship]], where he scored the first goal in the final even though he was the youngest player on the squad, and captained the team during the [[1999 FIFA World Youth Championship|1999 edition]].

Cambiasso made his Argentina senior national debut in 2000. He participated in the [[2005 FIFA Confederations Cup]] with his national side, a tournament in which Argentina reached the final. On 15 May 2006, he was named in the Argentina national team for the [[2006 FIFA World Cup|2006 World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/world_cup_2006/teams/argentina/default.stm |title=World Cup 2006: Argentina |publisher=BBC Sport |date=28 December 2006 |access-date=5 April 2014 }}</ref> On 16 June, he capped a 24-pass Argentine interplay with a finish to score the second goal in a [[2006 FIFA World Cup Group C#Argentina vs Serbia and Montenegro|6–0 victory]] over [[Serbia and Montenegro national football team|Serbia and Montenegro]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://espnfc.com/blog/_/name/worldcupcentral/id/3284?cc=5901 |title=World Cup's Greatest Goals: Esteban Cambiasso (2006, ARGENTINA vs. Serbia and Montenegro) |publisher=ESPNFC |date=4 April 2014 |access-date=5 April 2014 }}</ref> In the quarter-finals match against [[Germany national football team|Germany]] on 30 June 2006, the match went into penalties, where Cambiasso had his penalty kick saved, resulting in Argentina losing 4–2 and Germany progressing to the semi-final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/world_cup_2006/4991602.stm |title=Germany beat Argentina 4–2 in a penalty shoot-out after a tense quarter-final in Berlin ended 1–1 after extra-time. |publisher=BBC Sport |date=30 June 2006 |access-date=5 April 2014 }}</ref> The following year, he represented his country at the [[2007 Copa América]], where Argentina reached the final, losing out to South American rivals [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]].

Since [[Diego Maradona]] took over as Argentina coach, Cambiasso was only called-up once to the national team for a friendly game on 14 November 2009 against [[Spain national football team|Spain]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2009/nov/16/spain-argentina-friendly |title=Spain reign supreme despite Argentina's rough and tumble |work=The Guardian |date=14 November 2009 |access-date=28 August 2014 }}</ref> despite continuing to play a vital role for Inter in their treble-winning season, and re-affirming his status as one of Europe's best central midfielders. On 12 May 2010, Cambiasso and Inter teammate [[Javier Zanetti]] were controversially left out of the 30-man provisional [[2010 FIFA World Cup|2010 World Cup]] squad for Argentina.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2010/may/12/javier-zanetti-esteban-cambiasso-argentina-squad |title=Javier Zanetti and Esteban Cambiasso out of Argentina World Cup squad |work=The Guardian |date=12 May 2010 |access-date=5 April 2014 }}</ref>

On 20 August 2010, new Argentina coach [[Sergio Batista]] recalled Cambiasso to the national team for the friendly against newly crowned world champions Spain. Argentina handed Spain their first defeat since becoming world champions the month prior, earning a resounding 4–1 win in a friendly at the [[Estadio Monumental Antonio Vespucio Liberti|Monumental Stadium]] in Buenos Aires.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/world_cup_2010/8676659.stm|title=Coloccini fails to make cut for Argentina party|date=19 May 2010|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=16 June 2010}}</ref> Cambiasso also played for Argentina in the [[2011 Copa América]] on home soil, where they were eliminated by eventual champions [[Uruguay national football team|Uruguay]], on penalties, in the quarter-finals.

==Style of play==
Cambiasso was primarily a [[central midfielder]], capable of playing as a [[Defensive midfielder|defensive]] or [[box-to-box midfielder]]. Cambiasso was also deployed occasionally as a playmaking [[Sweeper (association football)|sweeper]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcinternews.it/angolo-tattico/cambiasso-fa-il-chivu-nella-difesa-a-tre-coutinho-94116|title=Cambiasso fa il Chivu nella difesa a tre. Coutinho...|publisher=F.C.InterNews.it|language=it|access-date=3 December 2014}}</ref> He was left-footed and known for his passing range, tactical intelligence, and ability to distribute the ball and create chances.<ref name="Cambiasso, da Serra Riccò al centrocampo nerazzurro">{{cite web|url=https://www.ilgiornale.it/news/cambiasso-serra-ricc-centrocampo-nerazzurro.html|title=Cambiasso, da Serra Riccò al centrocampo nerazzurro|date=10 March 2006 |publisher=Il Giornale|language=it|access-date=3 December 2014}}</ref><ref name="Champions, l'Inter non tradisce">{{cite web|url=http://www.sportmediaset.mediaset.it/calcio/articoli/articolo30217.shtml|title=Champions, l'Inter non tradisce|publisher=Mediaset|language=it|access-date=3 December 2014|archive-date=22 September 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140922020907/http://www.sportmediaset.mediaset.it/calcio/articoli/articolo30217.shtml|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.interclubcambiassotaranto.it/?page_id=12|title=Inter: Il nostro idolo Esteban Cambiasso|website=interclubcambiassotaranto.it|language=it|access-date=3 December 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fifa.com/womensworldcup/legends/esteban-cambiasso |title=Esteban Cambiasso |publisher=FIFA.com |access-date=14 April 2020 }}{{dead link|date=October 2021|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> His role has been likened to that of a [[Midfielder#Centre-half|''metodista'']], a midfielder who can dictate play while also contributing defensively.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/Squadre/Inter/13-11-2013/inter-cambiasso-vogliamo-arrivare-piu-alto-possibile-ce-metteremo-tutta-201563329376.shtml |title=Inter, Cambiasso: "Vogliamo arrivare il più in alto possibile. Ce la metteremo tutta" |work=La Gazzetta dello Sport |language=it |date=13 November 2013 |access-date=15 February 2024 }}</ref>

''[[Eurosport]]'' said about Cambiasso, when [[José Mourinho]] was still managing Inter, "There is nothing glamorous about the bald Argentine, but he is the heartbeat of the Inter side that have become the dominant force in Italian football. Just the kind of determined, hard-running midfielder José Mourinho loves. Originally a destroyer, the 29-year-old has become increasingly adventurous from an offensive standpoint, and weighs in with six to eight goals per season."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://uk.eurosport.yahoo.com/09072009/58/top-50-players-40-31.html |title=Top 50 players: 40–31 – Yahoo! Eurosport UK |publisher=Yahoo! |access-date=29 June 2010}}</ref>

[[Goal (website)|Goal]] said, "All in all, this player is one of the greatest players to have ever pulled an Inter shirt on and to grace the pitch in the Serie A. He is an intelligent midfielder, who has the capacity to change the shape of a game off his own boot. He is one of the most influential midfielders in Italian football, and for that reason and many more, he will certainly be remembered as one of the most talented players of all time."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/1717/editorial/2008/12/31/1034678/the-goalcom-50-esteban-cambiasso-29 |title=The Goal.com 50: Esteban Cambiasso (29) |publisher=Goal.com |author=Editorial |date=31 December 2008 |access-date=30 June 2010}}</ref> In 2017, Sean Lunt of ''The Versed'' pronounced him one of the most under-rated players of the last 15 years.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theversed.com/69632/esteban-cambiasso-underrated-legend-15-years/#.cCkZOlXaj5|title=Esteban Cambiasso: The most underrated legend of the last 15 years|publisher=The Versed|author=Sean Lunt|date=8 September 2017|access-date=31 March 2019}}</ref>

==Personal life==
[[File:Esteban Cambiasso.jpg|thumb|upright|Cambiasso in a picture taken by a fan]]

Cambiasso has a daughter and a son. On 22 November 2008, his wife Claudia gave birth to their daughter Victoria before Cambiasso's match for Inter against [[Juventus FC|Juventus]].<ref>{{cite web |author=Inter.it staff, inter(a t)inter.it |url=http://inter.it/aas/news/reader?N=30306&L=en&IDINI=30325 |title=F.C. Internazionale Milano |publisher=Inter.it |date=22 November 2008 |access-date=30 June 2010 |archive-date=10 August 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110810091259/http://www.inter.it/aas/news/reader?N=30306&L=en&IDINI=30325 |url-status=dead }}</ref> After Inter won the ''[[Derby d'Italia]]'', Cambiasso dedicated the win to his daughter.<ref>{{cite web |author=Inter.it staff, inter(a t)inter.it |url=http://inter.it/aas/news/reader?N=30313&L=en&IDINI=30325 |title=F.C. Internazionale Milano |publisher=Inter.it |date=22 November 2008 |access-date=30 June 2010 |archive-date=14 September 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110914101845/http://www.inter.it/aas/news/reader?N=30313&L=en&IDINI=30325 |url-status=dead }}</ref> His son Dante was born on 24 September 2013.<ref>{{cite web |author=Inter.it staff, inter(a t)inter.it |url=http://www.inter.it/en/news/43778 |title=F.C. Internazionale Milano |publisher=Inter.it |date=24 September 2013 |access-date=18 May 2015 |archive-date=13 June 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150613172022/http://www.inter.it/en/news/43778 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Two days later, Cambiasso scored a goal against Fiorentina and dedicated it to his family.<ref>{{cite web |author=Inter.it staff, inter(a t)inter.it |url=http://www.inter.it/en/news/43802 |title=F.C. Internazionale Milano |publisher=Inter.it |date=26 September 2013 |access-date=18 May 2015 |archive-date=13 June 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150613171248/http://www.inter.it/en/news/43802 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
